note: MP ice area page says 'still needs input', Judith Pond page has no directions; WTA/MP rock pages describe other Ancient Lakes and Quincy Lakes lots, none tied to the ice lines.
No page found for this crag on MP or elsewhere; searches only reach Nada Lake and Toketie Wall in the Enchantments, which do not match the stored coordinate.

trailheadDirection: From Seattle on US 2, turn left at Coles Corner and follow that road about 10 miles, then turn right onto White River Road and drive roughly 1.5 miles to a pullout on the left (the winter parking).
approach: From the White River Road winter pullout, cross to the right side of the road and follow the short trail, watching for a blue marker beside it; the crag sits about 200 feet from the road.
note: MP area page for the crag itself gives drive, winter pullout and 200 ft walk; no second page found.
No page found for this boulder area; searches for Rabbit Ridge / Dog Park boulders return nothing.

trailheadDirection: Take I-90 Exit 38 and follow the road all the way around, passing under the I-90 overpass, to the Dirty Harry's Peak trailhead lot; a Discover Pass is needed to park.
approach: From the Dirty Harry's Peak trailhead lot, follow the trail (or the fire academy road) over the bridge and bear right, about 15 minutes to the big leaning cedar at the start of Wayne's World. Walk back up beneath Darkside; Erikland is just to the right of Darkside.
note: Erikland page gives the access (cedar at start of Wayne's World, then under Darkside); Wayne's World page gives 15 min from the Farside trailhead; Exit 38 page identifies the Far Side parking lot and Discover Pass. Farside trailhead = Dirty Harry's lot is an inference from the Exit 38 page.

trailheadDirection: From the Mazama store, drive about 3.1 miles up Lost River Road to the Goat Wall Creek drainage and pull off nearby.
approach: From the Goat Wall Creek drainage pullout, hike uphill in the drainage, which narrows and gets brushy. Allow roughly 30 to 40 minutes depending on snow; the ice climb is the right-most one in this area.
note: The Standard route page (GPS identical to the stored crag coordinate) gives the drive, parking at the drainage and the walk; other routes on the crag (Goat's Beard Ice, Claymore) have no approach text.

trailheadDirection: From US 2 at Leavenworth, drive up Icicle Creek Road to the Bridge Creek Campground junction, which is where the plowed road ends in winter.
approach: From the Bridge Creek Campground junction, follow the dirt road over the bridge to a gate on the right, go past it for about 100 feet, then turn uphill to the left toward the falls. The upper half is a steep slope of 30 to 45 degrees that avalanches often.
note: MP Hubba Hubba area page gives parking and walk; Icicle ice area page agrees the climbs are off Icicle Creek Road via US-2 through Leavenworth. No mileage from a fetched page, so none stated.

trailheadDirection: On State Route 17 between US 2 and I-90, drive to milepost 82 on the west side of Lake Lenore.
approach: From the SR 17 milepost 82 pullout, the easiest way is to walk across the lake when it is frozen, then hike the hillside up into the gully holding the flow.
note: Only the Guiness route page gives milepost 82 and the lake crossing; Rainier Light overlooks Soap Lake and may start elsewhere, so low for the whole crag.
MP Lichen Rock page (Minnehaha) has no getting-there text and lists different problems; Minnehaha page gives only the drive to John Shields Park, no walk to this boulder.

trailhead: Dutch Henry Falls trailhead pullout (Jameson Lake Road)
trailheadDirection: From Wenatchee, drive east on US 2 past Waterville and Douglas and the junction with SR 182, then about 8 miles farther turn left on paved Jameson Lake Road; the north trailhead is about 4 miles along on the left, marked by a small preserve sign.
approach: From the Dutch Henry Falls trailhead pullout (Jameson Lake Road), follow the roughly half-mile path through open shrub-steppe to the creek below the falls, where the ice forms. The land is a conservation preserve, so no motor vehicles.
note: Sundance Kid is Dutch Henry Falls (4 mi up Jameson Lake Rd); WTA and a second guide agree on the pullout and short walk to the base of the falls; Butch Cassidy and Wild Bunch pages have no location text.

trailhead: Excelsior Campground road pullout (Mount Baker Highway milepost 40)
trailheadDirection: Drive east on the Mount Baker Highway (SR 542) to milepost 40 and park off the pavement on the old road to the closed Excelsior Campground and pump house.
approach: From the Excelsior Campground road pullout (Mount Baker Highway milepost 40), walk back west along the highway to the trail directly opposite milepost 40 and follow it uphill to the crag, staying on the path to spare the moss.
note: MP area page and a guide-service write-up agree on milepost 40 parking and the trail across the highway.
MP page gives only 'south of Devils Punchbowl, north of Zenith'; no parking or walk; no other page found.

Remote alpine peak in the Gunsight Range; fetched pages give no approach to the base of the named routes (approach is a two-day walk from the Blue Glacier side per search snippets only, not a fetched page).
Only summit-hike pages (Mirror Lake route, FS Road 5480) were found; none describe where the named routes begin, so no base-of-route walk.

trailheadDirection: Drive US 2 through Tumwater Canyon to any roadside pullout near milepost 94, where the flow can be seen from the road.
approach: From the US 2 pullouts near milepost 94, find a safe way across the river, which is the main obstacle and may not be frozen at its slow stretches. Follow the bank to the Fall Creek drainage and hike up it through avalanche terrain, about 2 hours to Drury Falls; The Pencil is in the same drainage several hundred yards to the west.
note: Drury Falls and The Pencil pages (GPS matches the crag) give pullout, river crossing and drainage; Comic Book Hero and The Drip are elsewhere in the canyon (across from Castle Rock, near the dam) and are not covered.
